name: Jujube (Ziziphus jujuba) syrup
short: Few data; syrup by mouth only. Children (constipation): no adverse events or liver or kidney injury reported. Tuberculosis pilot: no liver toxicity. Urticaria trial: minimal side effects, no figures.
text: These data are for syrups made from jujube (Ziziphus jujuba), taken by mouth; they do not cover the whole fruit eaten with its stone, the seed, or other preparations. In a double-blind randomized trial in children aged 2 to 10 with functional constipation, jujube syrup was compared with polyethylene glycol, a laxative, for 3 months, and liver and kidney function tests and blood sugar were checked at the start and end; a few self-limiting side effects were reported only in the polyethylene glycol group (30 children completed follow-up on jujube syrup), and the authors reported no adverse events or liver or kidney injury with the syrup, while saying further studies are needed to find potential side effects. In a small pilot placebo-controlled trial of jujube syrup in people with pulmonary tuberculosis on anti-tuberculosis drugs (8 completed on jujube, 9 on placebo), drug-induced liver toxicity developed in 27.3% of the placebo group by the second week and in none of the jujube group (the abstract does not give the number of patients behind the 27.3%, which cannot be a share of the 9 who completed); the abstract does not report other adverse events or name the jujube species. In a 28-day randomized double-blind trial of jujube oxymel (a jujube syrup preparation whose other ingredients the abstract does not give) taken with cetirizine, followed by 4 weeks of cetirizine alone, in 92 people aged 12 to 65 with chronic spontaneous urticaria, the authors mention minimal side effects without giving figures, and the abstract does not name the jujube species. The syrup was taken alongside anti-tuberculosis drugs in one trial and with the antihistamine cetirizine in another; neither abstract reports an interaction between them, and no other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
